transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Miles Ortega (Redwood SE), Dana Li (Peregrine Procurement), Priya Kapoor (Peregrine Legal), Marcus O'Neal (Peregrine Infosec), Samir Shah (Platform)

Summary: Quick procurement + legal checkpoint to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, KMS/BYOK expectations, egress pricing and pilot scope. Action items and deadlines captured.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA encryption/KMS, SOC2/ISO evidence, pricing tiers and egress, pilot scope (3 weeks), dedicated vs hosted options, escrow / escrow retention, SSO and SAML integration, audit logs retention, certified subprocessors.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. We'll run through the legal and procurement items first then hit the technical bits. Miles is on for infra questions.
[00:20] Dana Li: Great, thanks. For procurement side — we need to understand whether there are any hard minimums on committed spend, and how egress is calculated, especially for embeddings exports.
[00:34] Miles Ortega: Yeah so from Redwood's perspective, hosted API is usage-based, no long term minimums for the hosted tier, but Dedicated or Private does come with reserved capacity contracts — typically monthly or annual commits. For a pilot we can do a short reserved window or a trial cap.
[00:55] Priya Kapoor: On the legal side, our standard playbook requires an MSA and a DPA. We'll likely push for stronger data residency language and a customer-controlled KMS/BYOK model. Is that supported?
[01:12] Miles Ortega: We support BYOK integration for Private deployments today; for Hosted we have KMS integration options — customer-managed keys via a partner KMS/HSM is on the roadmap but we do support a bring-your-own-key flow for Dedicated in many cases. I'll send the checklist.
[01:34] Marcus O'Neal: Important: audit logs retention — we need at least one year of detailed audit logs for compliance. What are current retention defaults?
[01:45] Avery Chen: Default logs retention is 90 days for the console; extended retention is available as an add-on and can be configured to 12 months or more depending on plan. That would be part of the Private/support contract.
[02:05] Dana Li: Egress — are there fixed per-GB charges, or is egress bundled into token pricing? Our legal team flagged potential surprise costs on egress for large model outputs.
[02:18] Miles Ortega: Egress is typically billed separately if data leaves our cloud region; for many customers it's small relative to token spend, but for high-volume embedding exports or model offloading it can be material. We'll provide a calculator for your expected volumes.
[02:35] Samir Shah: For the pilot, we plan to run two workloads: real-time chat (~200 concurrent users) and nightly embedding exports (about 5TB/month). If egress is charged per-GB that's a big deal.
[02:52] Avery Chen: Understood, Samir. For pilot pricing we'll model both scenarios and show a Dedicated reserved option vs hosted bursts. Typically Dedicated reduces per-token unit cost and gives predictable throughput so egress predictability is easier to manage.
[03:10] Priya Kapoor: On the MSA, we have two immovable items: indemnity caps tied to fees and a data residency clause requiring EU data to remain in EU regions. Can Redwood sign those?
[03:24] Avery Chen: We can discuss indemnity cap tiers aligned to order size. Data residency — hosted can be region-pinned to EU region endpoints; Private gives full control. We'll flag those for legal.
[03:40] Dana Li: Also, do you support SOC2 Type II reports and ISO attestation? We'll need evidence for our vendor review.
[03:52] Miles Ortega: Yes — SOC2 Type II, plus ISO 27001 certificates are available. I'll share the latest reports. Note: some customer names in those reports are redacted.
[04:06] Marcus O'Neal: Subprocessors: can you provide the list and any subcontractors used for telemetry or logging? We need clarity for our DPA.
[04:18] Miles Ortega: We'll pull the current subprocessors list. Telemetry third parties are limited; storage and observability providers are typical cloud providers.
[04:30] Dana Li: Pricing question — what is the model for committed discounts? We have finance-driven thresholds for a preferred vendor.
[04:41] Avery Chen: Committed spend gets stepped discounts and guarantees on latency/SLOs in Dedicated. We can lay out a tiered pricing sheet — pilot -> POC -> committed. For procurement, we usually propose a 6–12 month pilot with a break/clawback clause.
[04:58] Samir Shah: Technical: if we choose Private and BYOK, how do you handle KV or KV cache encryption — is the cache stored encrypted with our keys?
[05:12] Miles Ortega: The KV cache and persistent caches can be encrypted at rest with customer keys in Private. In Hosted, transient KV is encrypted with our keys; bring-your-own-key for persistent storage is available for Dedicated/Private. There's a nuance around live KV in memory which is not persisted.
[05:34] Priya Kapoor: Regarding escrow — our compliance group asked whether source-escrow for the runtime is required. Is there an escrow offering?
[05:46] Avery Chen: We don't typically do source escrow for hosted customers. For large enterprise Private deals, there are options for an escrow arrangement — we can outline terms. Often customers accept documented runbooks + support SLAs instead.
[06:05] Dana Li: SLA specifics — uptime SLO, latency p50/p95 goals, and credits. We need the SLA language to be explicit in the MSA.
[06:18] Avery Chen: SLA language is standard but we can provide explicit p50/p95 and credits schedule. For Dedicated we provide SLA-backed latency windows. We'll include that as an exhibit.
[06:33] [crosstalk] Speaker 3: sorry, I'm on mute —
[06:36] Samir Shah: —I was going to say, do you provide canary/rollout tooling so we can mitigate model regressions during production rollouts?
[06:47] Miles Ortega: Yes — our console supports canaries and automatic fallback to previous model variants and region routing. We'll demo that in the technical kickoff.
[07:02] Priya Kapoor: A couple of data protection specifics: deletion timeframes for PII on request, right to audit, and contractually guaranteed deletion paths. We need those stated.
[07:15] Miles Ortega: We expose purge APIs and can include contractual deletion SLA — e.g., 30 days to purge persistent storage and 90 days for logs by default on hosted unless otherwise specified. We'll formalize in DPA language.
[07:30] Dana Li: One more procurement ask — can you accept our standard ecommerce payment terms or do you require vendor onboarding with Net30 / Net45?
[07:41] Avery Chen: We can be flexible but enterprise deals often follow Net30/Net45; for platform credits and reserved capacity we do invoicing monthly. We'll align with finance during contracting.
[07:55] Marcus O'Neal: Are there export control / data transfer restrictions we should be aware of? We operate in EMEA and APAC — data sovereignty matters.
[08:06] Miles Ortega: We can region-pin and for Private deployments you control the infrastructure. For hosted, cross-region failover is optional and can be restricted by policy. We'll document regions and constraints.
[08:20] Dana Li: Ok, moving to timeline — we want pilot results and procurement decision within 6 weeks. Is that realistic?
[08:29] Avery Chen: Yes — 3-week technical pilot + 1 week for evaluation + 1–2 weeks contracting is doable if DPA/MSA redlines are small. If many legal redlines, it can extend.
[08:42] Priya Kapoor: We'll try to keep redlines focused. One ask — can you deliver a DPA that includes specific subprocessor notification windows (30 days) and a clause for 3rd-party audits?
[08:55] Miles Ortega: Noted — we'll include subprocessor notification language.
[09:02] Samir Shah: For the pilot SOW can you include success criteria: <5% error rate on embeddings, p95 latency below 300ms for chat, and stable throughput at 200rps?
[09:15] Avery Chen: Absolutely. We'll draft an SOW with measurable criteria and acceptance tests.
[09:25] Dana Li: Anything on insurance or cyber liability — we may ask for a specific limit.
[09:33] Avery Chen: We carry cyber liability insurance; we'll share the certificate and limits. For higher limits, we can discuss endorsements.
[09:44] Priya Kapoor: Ok, that's helpful. We'll compile our list of DPA redlines and send to Avery.
[09:51] Avery Chen: Great — to recap next steps: I'll send the MSA/DPA draft with redlineable doc, Miles will share SOC2/ISO and infra diagram, and we'll get you a pilot pricing sheet including egress scenarios. Schedule: pilot kickoff 2027-04-28. Any objections?
[10:10] Dana Li: No objections. We'll aim to return legal godlines by 04-25.
[10:17] Samir Shah: I'll send expected traffic numbers today so you can model egress.
[10:22] Marcus O'Neal: We'll want a 30-minute technical pre-kickoff with your SEs the week of 04-26.
[10:31] Avery Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and attach the items discussed.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors (Speaker 3 noted), some product names transcribed as 'KV cash' etc. Natural speech hesitations and overlaps present.
